description: Construction of a two-storey extension at the lower and raised ground floor levels, the installation of three rooflights on the rear roof slope, and adjustments to the rear garden landscaping.
decision_conditions: <p><span id="docs-internal-guid-7fb3f876-7fff-6bdd-2560-91ea8eb9c67c"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, sans-serif; background-color: transparent; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline; white-space-collapse: preserve;">Insufficient information, specifically, an Overheating Risk Assessment, has been provided to allow for an assessment of policies SI 2 (Minimising greenhouse gas emissions), and SI 4 (Managing heat risk) of the London Plan (2021), and policies LP54 (Overheating and Adapting to Climate Change) and LP55 (Mitigating Climate Change) of the Hackney Local Plan LP33 (2020). Therefore, the application has not satisfactorily demonstrated that the scheme will mitigate the risk of overheating and the reliance on active cooling systems as required by the abovementioned policies.</span></span></p>

<p><span id="docs-internal-guid-6c2f4de3-7fff-9941-fab2-9015ac313b75"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, sans-serif; background-color: transparent; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline; white-space-collapse: preserve;">Insufficient arboricultural information has been provided to allow for an assessment of the impacts of the proposal on the trees present on the site and adjoining land. Therefore, the application has not satisfactorily demonstrated that the application will not cause harm to trees in a conservation area to the detriment of the visual amenities of the site, contrary to policies LP46 (Protection and Enhancement of Green Infrastructure), LP47 (Biodiversity and Sites of Importance of Nature Conservation), and LP51 (Tree Management and Landscaping) of the Hackney Local Plan (2020) and policies G1 (Green infrastrucure), G6 (Biodiversity and access to nature), and G7 (Trees and woodlands) of the London Plan (2021). </span></span></p>

<p><span id="docs-internal-guid-5db51adf-7fff-1e51-243f-ee4b45fdb98c"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, sans-serif; background-color: transparent; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline; white-space-collapse: preserve;">By reason of its inappropriate size, scale, and materials, the proposed rear extension would result in an obtrusive and incongruous development that would detract from the architectural integrity of the existing building as well as the wider row of terraced properties of which the application site forms part. As such, the proposal would fail to preserve or enhance the character and appearance of the Graham Road and Mapledene Conservation Area. This identified less than substantial harm would not be outweighed by any public benefits. The proposed development would, therefore, conflict with policies D3 (Optimising site layout through the design-led approach), D4 (Delivering good design), and HC1 (Heritage conservation and growth) of the London Plan (2021) and policies LP1 (Design Quality and Local Character) and LP3 (Designated Heritage Assets) of the Hackney Local Plan 2033 (2020) and the advice in Hackney's Residential Extensions and Alterations SPD (2009). </span></span></p>
